eject cclio gazette from cw (for now): Yesterday I was printing messages to a co-work thread and discovered an interesting thing. A gazette gets seeded into a separate memory leaf in co-work memory topics but it appears that co-work auto-loads into his memory in each thread. Only two memory leaves are loaded into memory: preferences and some other data I can't recall currently, and all other custom memory leaves are read-only when needed. It appeared due to the specifics of the gazette.

It appears to be one of the least interesting memory leaves to auto-load for regular co-work, especially in the way I use it, because essentially I use it very rarely to solve fleet-related questions. I primarily use co-work for games, for engineering research, and for cooking, and for some other questions about my phone or other smaller stuff.

It appears that the gazette is useful primarily for you to be aware of what we were doing for the recent few days and in compact shape it works better than when we previously loaded it into your memory in full shape.

TLDR: what I ask about is to eject Cleo gazette from co-work memory fully. You can't delete memory, if that's up to me. I will delete the gazette memory from co-work memory and your part is to ensure that all parts of gazette delivery to co-work are deleted everywhere, with all tails, which are a memory sync skill. You also have special fields for co-work seeding the gazette in each gazette. I think you can delete them too. 

Also I can't recall precisely but you have some script also for daily scheduled gazette updating co-work. It is currently active. My part is to disable it, delete it, and your part is to delete all the scripting that compiles gazette delivery for that scheduled task.

the chords app: when i change a hotkey binding that you are not aware of (cant access, e.g. raycast) — i want an ability to reassing tracking hotkey from that app UI. like for example i switch hyper+e from linear to hyper+l. to not loop it over you - i simply rebind via UI myself. will it work? also, surface editing would be good. e.g. Linear raycast  to anything else. 
note: this is better to do after coder migrates an app to vite.

evergreen weekly: how to pull non-brew changelogs to your weekly update notice list? like [raycast](https://www.raycast.com/changelog) for example - it gets self updated and you are not aware of the changes. let's integrate into evergreen an «invisible» changelogs listing. things like raycast for example. maybe not all apps i use but ones i use the most. i provide you few names, you hunt reliable link to read changes from, likely store a timestamp of previous evergreen and then each weekly evergreen you diff the delta and tell what interesting appeared. DOT-232 is also about that, but a bit easier for you because it is your [own changelogs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog). let's make it work and resolve DOT-232 before monday's evergreen so we will test drive this flow on monday sept 21.
why: i want to know about interesting updates in software i am interested in, but there is too many updates evertywhere so you will release a comprehensive shortlist of everything interesting for me.

jev: how to properly integrate his flows?  for example we create a new flow for jev —  a coder retro breakdown as planned. This is purely an example. It could be anything new, even considering our existing flows, using Jelforce as a skill router and as an inbox item triager for any flow: how to make a job flow accepted, so to say, polished.

What I mean is, Jeff's initial precision is based on his config file of the flow that he uses and it purely depends on the precision of those prompts and the details provided to him to do things. Before accepting Gel Flow as automated and treated as reliable, a flow first needs to be sharpened.

How to correctly and reliably have this process of moving a job from an idea phase to a phase when this flow is considered reliable and doesn't want to be overseen too much?

 I think we need to introduce some validation criteria because, mostly, Jelf is your tool that you have to use to unload yourself. Along with that, Jelf's output must be reliable and he is not allowed to produce false negatives. To do that you have to oversee and sharpen each Jelf's flow before it is considered reliable and likely each flow also needs some tracking file with history for it. For example we create a flow and that flow receives a log file with Jelf's performance. You iterate on sharpening Jelf's flow and set a vet, for example, for 1 week, and you continue or observe Jelf's performance on one or another flow. After Jelf produces no issues for 1 week, for example, that flow is considered green (passed) and the vet is raised on that flow.
 
  and if during that period of 1 week Jelf produces some error in his flow, then that 1-week period gets renewed from the moment the error occurred. A his vet week is a shifted window that resets on each error. will this work? or you already setup his reinforcement/sharpening this way?
